name: Bun cha ca
summary: Fish cake in a broth of fish bone and fish head, usually tuna or sailfish rather than pork, with a chili sauce particular to Binh Dinh. The broth is gently sweet and not fishy, and fried and steamed cakes share the bowl.
origin: Quy Nhon. Bowls are eaten on Nguyễn Huệ in the center.
texture: Fried cake and steamed cake share the bowl: soft and smooth from the round and steamed pieces, chewy from the fried piece.
taste: The broth is gently sweet. The tuna or sailfish bone broth is naturally sweet, rich, and not fishy, and the dip is chili sauce with pickled shallot.
howToEat: Dip the cake in the chili sauce, keep the herbs in the bowl, and take a sip of broth with each bite.

The herbs are lettuce, shredded cabbage, a few banana-flower strands, bean sprouts, and mint, with pickled shallot beside the chili. Some cooks put chopped scallion and dill in the cake. Others leave the dill out.
where: Nguyễn Huệ, in the center. Number 26 is the provincial museum, not a stall.
seoTitle: Bun cha ca — Quy Nhon fish-cake noodles
seoDescription: Quy Nhon bún chả cá: fried and steamed fish cake in a sweet tuna or sailfish bone broth, with Binh Dinh chili sauce and a plate of herbs.
